report:
Where things stand: the three coworkers validated **Option 1 only as a brief pause, not a solution**. I am stopping here, as A, B and C each asked for no further follow-up/confirmations. No repair, replacement, purchase, disposal, ownership/legal decision, money movement, rota, cleanup assignment, or new tending was agreed.

**Confirmed NCEs (recorded only after each person said the wording fits):**
- Shared/process, confirmed by A, B, C and me as a participant: “We want clarity and room for honest disagreement”; “We want the shared list to stay open to correction”; “We want any plan to stay within choices we can actually make here.”
- A: effort of using/sorting the setup fitting people’s actual energy (incl. avoiding repairs or a rota); enough clarity about the leak to understand what we’re dealing with; shared equipment easy for everyone to use and clean up after; parts that still work considered with care; personal meaning having room to be spoken honestly; everyone free from pressure to agree; each person’s stated concerns received as their own, not as a claim about everyone; conversation brief enough to respect people’s energy; “We want room to disagree without having to explain at length.”
- B: personal and family meaning treated with care; effort around shared equipment sustainable; time/pace fitting actual availability; each person’s own reasons understood on their own terms. B later said “not keep wearing me down,” repeated checking, “don’t make me explain or speak for A,” and extra chasing are covered by those plus A’s brevity/room-to-disagree lines — no separate unconfirmed wording added. B’s “no known grinder problem” was explicitly an observation, not a concern.
- C: everyday coffee arrangement dependable; shared workspace calm; practical problems affecting daily use recognized as mattering; everyone has a say without anyone placed in the middle; coordinating the conversation clear without resting on one coworker; “We want the grinder acknowledged as part of the setup” (replaced my earlier “not quite” wording); brief-conversation wording fits.

**Draft options brought back for validation:** (1) acknowledge-and-pause; (2) optional already-available backup; (3) one-line already-known information. Every note invited “none,” “need change,” “not quite,” and even minor discomfort, and said a no would be added rather than overcome. I used only explicit replies; no silence counted as agreement.

**Validation:** All three can live with Option 1 as a brief pause: leak seriousness left unknown rather than guessed; grinder acknowledged without being turned into a preference or assumed compatible with a replacement; old machine and its family meaning honored and untouched; A’s simpler-machine view and B’s repair/keep view kept as their own; no final outcome; one brief validation then stop. Option 2 was not validated by all (A conditional only; B “Option 1 only”; C did not endorse). Option 3 was set aside: all three agreed with my participant objection that even that one-line request feels like another check. I also weighed the drafts against the list and said plainly that none fully delivers dependable everyday coffee; all three agreed it remains unresolved. My NCEs sat on the same list, not above anyone else’s.

**Unresolved, not papered over:** dependable everyday coffee; enough clarity about the leak; full ease/cleanup and sustainable-effort concerns; the substantive disagreement between a simpler low-tending machine and repairing/keeping the late father’s machine; grinder compatibility with any replacement (unknown fact); calm workspace and fairness only honored as process, not claimed settled. No hard deadline and no one tasked to chase or investigate.
